newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Thursday were light at $67.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00 that were not sold during Wednesday's heavy trade, feedlot sources said.
About 80,000 head sold Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area and about 60,000 in Kansas at $68.00, steady with most of last week's sales but up $1.00 from sales late last week.
Most cattle left were below the quality of cattle sold Wednesday and could sell at $67.00, some sources said.
There were reports that several loads of cattle sold Wednesday were being shipped early Thursday, reflecting some packers' short-bought status, sources said.
Firm beef demand underpinned fed cattle prices this week, market sources said.
Reported beef movement on Wednesday was heavy at slightly lower prices. Beef prices were quoted $0.10 to $0.35 per cwt lower on 370 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Beef movement for the week to date Wednesday totaled 827 fabricated loads, compared with 765 the previous week, USDA statistics showed.
